# Simulation data — regenerated by the user

The bulk of the per-run simulation outputs (`*.npy`, `*.npz`, `*.dat`, totalling roughly 7 GB for the canonical Halle / caudate Yaakub run) are **not** tracked in this repository. They are regenerated by running the pipeline stages documented in the top-level `README.md` (sections "Reproducing the manuscript" and "Data").

What lives in this tree:
- **`halle_caudate/`** — canonical Yaakub-on-Halle run.  When regenerated, this directory holds the FDTD pressure history (`propagation_map.npy`), the body-force field (`radiation_force.npy`), the shear-FDTD displacement (`displacement_4d.npy`, `displacement.npy`), the bioheat ΔT field (`bioheat/delta_T_*.npy`), and the per-voxel neural simulation outputs (`neural_results.npz`). The figures used by the manuscript are produced from these arrays.
- **`halle_caudate/validation_report/`** — standalone validation-report TeX/PDF and the constituent figures, plus the `manifest.json` and `thermal_metrics.json` metadata files that survive in git as small-file artefacts of each run.
- **`halle_caudate/bioheat/thermal_metrics.json` and `thermal_indices.json`** — small JSON metadata files (kept under version control as run-level provenance).
- **`halle_bowl/`, `halle_transcranial/`, `halle_transcranial_cfl0p4/`** — additional reference configurations.  Their large `*.npy` outputs are likewise gitignored; only the validation-report PDFs and small caches are tracked.
- **`fig8_cumulative_snapshots.npz`, `halle_mechanism_sweep_results.npz`, `sensitivity_results.npz`, `sensitivity_table.tex`** — outputs of the mechanism-sweep and sensitivity-sweep drivers (Stages 7 and 9). The `.tex` is tracked (auto-included in the manuscript); the `.npz` results are not, and re-generate cheaply from the canonical run plus the sweep scripts.

To regenerate the full data tree from scratch, run the stages listed in the top-level README in order. Stages 1 (acoustic FDTD) and 4 (Pennes bioheat) require the upstream `fullwave` and `shearwave` solvers. Stages 5+ (per-voxel neural simulation, mechanism sweep, sensitivity sweep, figure composites) depend only on this repository's package plus the saved displacement and temperature fields.
